title: Linear Extensive Game
body_html:
Linear Extensive Game

An extensive game is linear for player $i$ if no play intersects any information set of player $i$ more than once.

Linearity rules out repeated visits to the same information set along a single play, which is enough to compare behavioral and mixed strategies in one direction.

References

  • [MFoGT, Def. 6.3.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Linearity for a player means no play crosses one of that player's information sets more than once.
